originalStory:
--- Page 1 ---
„Wartet!", rief Daniel, noch halb hinter der Küchentür. Er drückte den beiden einen gefalteten Zettel in die Hand und verschwand sofort wieder — vermutlich, um seinen Kaffeebecher zu suchen.

Emma riss den Zettel auf. Darauf stand in großen, wackeligen Buchstaben: *Wo der alte Mann mit dem weißen Schnurrbart wohnt, wartet die nächste Aufgabe.*

„Das ist Hans!", sagte Noah. Er griff sich seinen Rucksack und war schon aus der Tür, bevor Emma den Zettel noch einmal gelesen hatte.

„Warte!" Emma rannte hinterher, den Zettel noch in der Hand. Diesmal wartete sie nicht auf ihn — sie wartete auf niemanden.

--- Page 2 ---
Hans stand an seinem Gartenzaun und schüttelte den Kopf. „Schatzsuche? Hier? Nein, nein, nein." Er lachte so laut, dass die Spatzen vom Dach flatterten.

Noah verschränkte die Arme. „Wir wissen, dass der Schatz bei dir ist. Der Zettel sagt es."

„Kein Schatz bei mir." Hans klopfte sich auf die Taschen seiner Strickjacke — und hielt inne. Er griff in die linke Tasche. Dann in die rechte. Dann zog er die Augenbrauen hoch und holte einen versiegelten Umschlag hervor.

„Vielleicht doch", sagte er.

Noah streckte die Hand aus. Hans hielt den Umschlag hoch, deutlich über Noahs Reichweite.

„Erst sagen: Bitte."

Noah seufzte tief, als käme das Wort aus einer sehr großen Tiefe. „Bitte."

--- Page 3 ---
Auf dem zweiten Zettel stand nur eines: *Keller.*

Die Kellertür war alt und schwer, und dahinter war es dunkel. Sehr dunkel.

Emma blieb stehen. Ihre Füße wollten nicht weiter. Noah drückte die Tür auf und schaute hinein. „Da drin ist er bestimmt", sagte er.

Emma sagte nichts. Sie starrte in das Schwarz hinter der Tür und hielt die Luft an.

Da sah sie es: Ein kleines Stück Papier war mit einem Stück Klebeband an den Türrahmen geklebt. Emmas Lippen bewegten sich lautlos, während sie las. *Halt die Tür mit dem Ziegelstein auf — der liegt rechts unten. Sarah.*

Emma bückte sich, fand den Ziegelstein und klemmte ihn vor die Tür. Licht fiel in den Keller. Nicht viel — aber genug.

Sie trat hinein.

--- Page 4 ---
Die Schatulle war aus dunklem Holz und hatte einen kleinen Messingverschluss. Emma und Noah trugen sie gemeinsam nach oben in den Garten.

Daniel stand schon dort, die Hände in den Taschen. Sarah kam kurz darauf und schob ihre Brille gerade. Hans trödelte hinterher. Er hatte seinen eigenen Schokoriegel dabei.

Noah öffnete den Verschluss. Im Inneren lagen alte Fotos, eine Tafel Schokolade und ein kleiner Zettel.

Emma las ihn laut vor: „*Abenteuer schmeckt am besten zusammen.*"

Noah betrachtete die Fotos eine Weile. Dann grinste er — nicht weil der Schatz aus Gold war, sondern weil er froh war, dass Emma dabei gewesen war.

Emma brach die Schokolade in Stücke. Die beiden saßen nebeneinander im Gras, und Hans legte seinen Riegel dazu.

*(Word count: 114)*

Generate a SINGLE illustration filling the ENTIRE canvas edge-to-edge. No borders, no frames, no margins, no white edges. No split screen, no panels, no grid, no collage. The artwork must extend to all four edges. All surfaces in the scene — walls, shutters, vehicles, garments, paper, screens, pole-mounted boards, shopfronts — render free of written characters, letters, numbers, or symbols, unless the scene description explicitly names the text to show. Character names from the prompt (e.g. labels like `[Noah]`, `[Emma]`) are reference identifiers only — never paint them onto clothing, signs, banners, captions, name tags, or any surface in the scene.

When the FIRST reference photo shows a real location (architecture, landscape, no characters in it), render the scene IN that location — copy its setting, architecture, geography, and lighting. All OTHER reference photos define each character's IDENTITY only — face, hair, skin tone, build, and clothing — never their pose, framing, or composition. Characters' positions, actions, body direction, and size come entirely from the scene description and the COMPOSITION rules below.

**Clothing for each named character (must match the attached labeled portrait):**
- Emma: soft pink long-sleeve top, dark navy blue dungarees with adjustable straps, white cotton socks, pale pink velcro trainers
- Noah: olive green crew-neck sweatshirt, mid-blue jeans with a small turn-up at the ankle, white lace-up sneakers, small red backpack worn on both shoulders
- Daniel: faded dark blue henley shirt with three buttons at the collar, mid-grey chinos, brown leather loafers

**HEIGHT ORDER (shortest to tallest):** Emma (shortest) -> Noah (taller) -> Daniel (noticeably taller)

Emma — a preschooler girl with average build, large head relative to body, soft rounded features, brown eyes, brown wavy ear-length hair in a ponytail with a side part on the right, freckles, and small stud earrings — stands in the foreground at the right side of a bright morning kitchen, both hands holding a small folded paper note open at chest height, her gaze fixed on the handwritten words. She faces slightly toward Noah in the midground. Noah — a kindergartner boy with average build, large head relative to body, soft rounded features, blue eyes, and blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs at his eyebrows — stands a step behind Emma toward the center of the kitchen, a small red backpack already slung over one shoulder, his body turned toward the kitchen door as if about to move. Daniel — an adult man with average build, adult proportions, mature bone structure, brown eyes, dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache — stands in the background near the half-open kitchen door, one hand still resting on the door frame, the other raised in a small wave. The kitchen behind them is warm and cluttered in a homey way: a wooden table with a checked tablecloth, a mug near the edge, morning light streaming in through a window above the sink. The scene is airy and cheerful, full of yellow-white morning light, the kind of ordinary kitchen that looks slightly larger than life when you are five years old. Wide shot, soft warm interior morning light, gentle adventurous mood.

**COMPOSITION:**
- Characters must INTERACT with the scene — facing and engaging with objects, landmarks, or each other. NOT standing in front of a backdrop looking at the viewer.
- Characters face TOWARD what they interact with. Eyes look at objects or other characters, NOT at the camera.
- If a character is INTERACTING with something in the BACKGROUND (running toward the castle, looking up at the tower, walking toward the bridge), they face that direction — back or side to the camera. If the character's interaction target is in foreground or midground, they face that target instead, with face visible to the reader.
- Each character must be DOING something specific (reaching, looking at, holding, walking toward). No static posing.
- **DEPTH — read each character's position label and honour it:** "foreground" characters fill roughly the lower half of the frame, large, with feet on the ground. "midground" characters occupy the MIDDLE BAND — heads do NOT reach the top edge, feet do NOT reach the bottom edge. "background" characters are small, distant, far behind. Foreground larger than midground larger than background.
- **KEEP THE FOREGROUND (LOWER STRIP) EMPTY** unless a character is explicitly labelled "foreground". When all characters are midground or background the bottom portion shows only the natural ground of this scene (cobblestones, floor, water, grass, sand, snow). When any character IS labelled foreground, that character's body and feet belong in this strip.

**ERFORDERLICHE OBJEKTE IN DIESER SZENE (MÜSSEN im Bild erscheinen):**
* **Familienküche** (location): indoor, residential kitchen. Colors: warm pine-yellow walls, pale terracotta tile floor, green-and-white checked tablecloth, white ceramic sink. wooden kitchen table in the center, cluttered shelf of mismatched mugs on the left wall, half-open door on the far right, window above the sink letting in morning light. Signature: forgotten coffee mug on the edge of the checked tablecloth
* **Erster Hinweiszettel** (object): A palm-sized square of white paper, folded once in half, with large wobbly handwritten black ink letters visible when unfolded; slightly creased at the fold

**ART STYLE:** A traditional watercolor painting in the style of Inga Moore. Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults. Textured paper with pencil underpainting, delicate color washes with wet-on-wet technique, soft paint edges, visible artistic brushstrokes, and luminous flowing colors. Characters are fully opaque — never see-through, never fading into the background. Warm but not overly vibrant color palette with visible paper texture throughout. Faces: watercolor wash rendering with visible brushstroke texture, age-appropriate features with defined bone structure. Eyes naturally sized. Never sharp or digitally rendered.


EXACT POSES:
- Emma: holds the folded note open at chest height, reading it
- Noah: reaches toward the kitchen door, rucksack over one shoulder

Emma — a preschooler girl with a large head relative to her small body, soft rounded features, brown eyes, brown wavy ear-length hair in a ponytail with a side part, freckles, and small stud earrings, wearing her standard outfit — stands in the foreground near the wooden kitchen table, both hands holding the small folded paper note open at chest height, her gaze dropped down onto the handwritten words on the page. She faces the table, body angled slightly away from the door. Noah — a kindergartner boy with a large head relative to his body, soft rounded features, blue eyes, and blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs at his eyebrows, wearing his standard outfit with a small red backpack slung over both shoulders — stands in the midground between Emma and the half-open kitchen door, his body turned fully toward the door, one foot already lifted as if mid-step toward the exit, his gaze directed at the doorway ahead of him. Daniel — an adult man with average build, dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, wearing his standard outfit — stands in the background at the half-open kitchen door, one hand resting on the door frame, the other raised in a small wave toward the two children, his gaze directed at Emma and Noah. The kitchen is the Familienküche: warm pine-yellow walls, pale terracotta tile floor, the wooden kitchen table at center with its green-and-white checked tablecloth, a forgotten coffee mug resting near the edge of the tablecloth, a cluttered shelf of mismatched mugs on the left wall, and morning light streaming through the window above the white ceramic sink. The note Emma holds is the Erster Hinweiszettel: a palm-sized square of white paper folded once, now open, with large wobbly handwritten black ink letters clearly visible on its surface — no additional text or pseudo-writing, only the letter shapes as a design element. Wide shot, soft yellow-white morning interior light, cheerful and slightly adventurous mood.

Beyond her left foot, the cellar drops into deep charcoal shadow; old glass jars on wooden shelves are barely visible at the far edges of that darkness. A band of warm late-morning sunlight falls from behind the camera across the stone threshold, lighting Emma's face and catching the white paper in her right hand. The torn scrap of paper is the focal point. Close-up shot.

bboxDetection.rawPrompt:
Detect the 2d bounding boxes of all figures and objects in this illustrated image.

EXPECTED CHARACTERS (identify by name if found):
1. Emma - Emma is a preschooler little girl (Looks: preschooler), average build. Hair: brown, wavy, ear-length, ponytail, side part right, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips, freckles, small stud earrings. Wearing: Pink long-sleeve t-shirt with a large blue and orange butterfly print on the front and sleeves, Dark blue skinny jeans, White sneakers with white laces
   Expected position: left foreground, kneeling on the lawn over the open box
2. Noah - Noah is a kindergartner little boy (Looks: kindergartner), average build. Hair: blonde, wavy, ear-length, bangs at eyebrows, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips. Wearing: Dark green hoodie with a large white T-Rex graphic on the front and a front pocket., Dark grey sweatpants with a drawstring waist., Blue sneakers with white soles and velcro straps.
   Expected position: right foreground beside Emma, kneeling, holding the note up
3. Daniel - Daniel is a adult man (Looks: adult), average build. Hair: dark brown, wavy, short. Facial hair: short beard, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips, beard, mustache. Wearing: dark blue long-sleeve button-up shirt, light brown chinos, dark brown leather lace-up shoes
   Expected position: midground behind and between Emma and Noah, standing
4. Sarah - Sarah is a adult woman (Looks: adult), average build. Hair: blonde, straight, chin-length, combed, side part left, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips. Glasses: rectangular dark-framed glasses. Wearing: White long-sleeved blouse with a round neckline., Dark blue pleated midi skirt with a subtle floral or abstract pattern., Black ballet flats.
   Expected position: midground slightly to Daniel's right, standing, facing the children
5. Hans - Hans is a elderly elderly man (Looks: elderly), average build. Hair: white, straight, short, combed. Facial hair: mustache, rounded jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips, prominent white mustache. Wearing: Red and black plaid long-sleeved button-up shirt, brown leather suspenders with a decorative chest piece, Brown corduroy pants, Brown lace-up shoes
   Expected position: background along the garden path, walking toward the group

EXPECTED OBJECTS (check if present):
- Hausgarten mit Zaun
- Schatzkiste
- Abschlusszettel
- Schokoriegel



COORDINATE SYSTEM:
- Values are 0-1000 (Gemini native format)
- Origin is top-left corner
- Format: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]

FIGURE COUNT LIMIT:
- Return AT MOST 10 figures total. If the scene has a crowd in the background, do NOT enumerate each crowd member as a separate figure — the crowd is backdrop, not a list.
- Only include a figure if its face OR body occupies at least ~5% of the frame width or height. Tiny silhouettes in the distance are backdrop, skip them.
- If you cannot distinguish between several figures (e.g. multiple blurred robes in the background), return ONE figure representing the group and set `name: "UNKNOWN"`, `label: "background crowd"` — never duplicate the same label across many entries.

FOR EACH FIGURE (up to 10, including partially visible ones near the edges of main subjects):
- If you can identify it as an expected character, set "name" to the character name (EXACTLY as listed above)
- Use CLOTHING + POSITION to distinguish figures (two figures with similar build are distinguished by what they wear and where they stand)
- If not identifiable as any expected character, set "name" to "UNKNOWN"
- Include "confidence": "high", "medium", or "low" for identification certainty
- face_box: bounding box around the head region.
  Include the top of the head and the bottom of the head outline, and the full width from side to side.
  Common mistakes to AVOID:
  * Do NOT cut off the top of the head — include the full head outline
  * Do NOT cut off the bottom of the head outline
  * Do NOT make the box too narrow — include the full head width
  * When in doubt, make the face_box LARGER rather than smaller
  * The face_box should be roughly square for a front-facing figure
- body_box: bounding box around the FULL FIGURE (or as much as visible)
- If the head is not visible (back view, non-human creature), set face_box to null

FOR EXPECTED OBJECTS:
- Report "found": true/false for each expected object
- If found, include body_box bounding box and position

LABEL LENGTH RULE (non-negotiable):
- Every `label` field MUST be ≤ 10 words.
- Name ONE defining clothing item + ONE distinguishing feature. Example: "boy in blue hoodie with backpack".
- DO NOT list everything the figure is wearing. DO NOT describe actions. DO NOT describe expressions.
- Long labels waste response tokens and cause the JSON to truncate before closing.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "figures": [
    {
      "name": "CharacterName or UNKNOWN",
      "label": "≤10 words — one defining item + one distinguishing feature",
      "position": "left|center|right",
      "face_box": [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] or null,
      "body_box": [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max],
      "confidence": "high|medium|low"
    }
  ],
  "objects": [
    {
      "name": "expected object name",
      "found": true|false,
      "label": "visual description if found",
      "position": "left|center|right",
      "body_box": [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] or null
    }
  ]
}

Given expected characters: "CharacterA (figure with blonde hair)" and "CharacterB (figure with brown curly hair)"
Given expected objects: "golden crown", "brown teddy bear"

  "figures": [
    {
      "name": "CharacterA",
      "label": "figure with blonde hair in blue hoodie",
      "position": "left",

      "face_box": [100, 680, 280, 830],
      "body_box": [90, 600, 680, 900],

    },
    {
      "name": "UNKNOWN",

      "face_box": null,
      "body_box": [500, 400, 700, 600],

    }

      "name": "golden crown",
      "found": true,
      "label": "golden crown on table",
      "position": "center",

    },
    {
      "name": "brown teddy bear",

      "label": null,

    }
  ]
}

IMPORTANT:
- Detect ALL visible figures, even if partially visible or UNKNOWN
- Be precise with bounding boxes — they will be used for inpainting
- Match figures by approximate BUILD first (short vs tall, slim vs broad), then use CLOTHING and POSITION to distinguish similar figures
- Two figures with similar build are distinguished by their outfits and scene position
- For creatures/animals/non-humans that are not expected characters, use "UNKNOWN"

Render this as an empty location backdrop. Foreground, midground and background bands all show the scene's natural ground/floor/water surface continuing unbroken — characters will be composited into them later. No figures, no animals.

**ABOUT THE LANDMARK REFERENCE PHOTO (when provided):** It is a real-world photograph, often taken recently. Use it for the landmark's shape, proportions, architecture, and camera angle only. Exclude any modern elements visible in the photo: cars, parked vehicles, traffic signs, road markings, street lights, utility poles, power lines, billboards, commercial advertising, shopfront windows with price tags, plastic bins, satellite dishes, air conditioners, modern pedestrians. Separate props sit in open space relative to the landmark — never mounted on or overlapping its structure.

Lighting must come from a consistent direction — all shadows point the same way.
The ground, floor, or surface where characters would stand or sit must be clearly visible.
The frame must leave enough physical space for characters to be composited into the scene naturally.
For `over-the-shoulder` framing, keep the centre-back of the frame visually open.
Use the camera angle named in the **SHOT** line above. Do not change the framing.

**ART STYLE:** A traditional watercolor painting in the style of Inga Moore. Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults. Textured paper with pencil underpainting, delicate color washes with wet-on-wet technique, soft paint edges, visible artistic brushstrokes, and luminous flowing colors. Characters are fully opaque — never see-through, never fading into the background. Warm but not overly vibrant color palette with visible paper texture throughout. Emma — a preschool-age girl with a round face, brown wavy ear-length hair pulled into a ponytail with a side part, freckles, and small stud earrings, wearing her standard clothes — kneels in the left foreground on the bright green lawn of the residential garden, both hands gripping the sides of the open dark walnut-stained wooden treasure box on the grass directly in front of her, the box lid standing upright at roughly ninety degrees, the faded red interior lining and contents visible; her gaze is directed straight down into the box. Noah — a kindergarten-age boy with a round face, blue eyes, blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs touching his eyebrows, wearing his standard clothes — kneels on the lawn beside Emma to her right, his right hand raising a small square of white paper to his eye level, his face turned toward the paper and eyes reading it. Daniel — a middle-aged man with average build, dark brown wavy short hair, brown eyes, short beard and mustache, wearing his standard clothes — stands upright on the lawn in the midground behind and between Emma and Noah, both arms loose at his sides, facing the two children. Sarah — a middle-aged woman with average build, blonde straight chin-length hair combed with a side part, blue eyes, rectangular dark-framed glasses, wearing her standard clothes — stands in the midground close to Daniel's right side, facing the children, her hands clasped together at waist height with fingers clearly separated and individually visible. Hans — an elderly man with average build, white straight short combed hair, a prominent white mustache, brown eyes, wearing his standard clothes — walks along the gravel garden path in the background toward the group, his right hand extended forward and slightly up, holding a palm-sized rectangular chocolate bar in a dark brown and gold foil wrapper at mid-chest height with the bar clearly visible flat across his palm, the bar's rectangular shape and wrapper detail fully legible; his left arm swings naturally at his side, elbow slightly bent, hand open and visible away from his torso. The garden setting is the Hausgarten mit Zaun: vivid green lawn, the low white wooden garden fence with slightly peeling paint running horizontally across the lower-middle distance, and at the far right edge of the frame a dense rectangular flower bed of small tightly packed orange marigolds forming a clear band of colour against the fence. Bright midday sunlight falls at a steep overhead angle, casting short hard-edged shadows directly beneath each figure on the grass; no soft diffused shadows. Warm celebratory mood. Ultra-wide shot.

   Expected position: right foreground beside Emma, kneeling, holding the note up
3. Daniel - Daniel is a adult man (Looks: adult), average build. Hair: dark brown, wavy, short.    Expected position: midground behind and between Emma and Noah, standing

Wearing: White long-sleeved blouse with a round neckline., Dark blue pleated midi skirt with a subtle floral or abstract pattern., Black ballet flats.
   Expected position: midground slightly to Daniel's right, standing, facing the children

Facial hair: mustache, rounded jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips, prominent white mustache. Wearing: Red and black plaid long-sleeved button-up shirt, brown leather suspenders with a decorative chest piece, Brown corduroy pants, Brown lace-up shoes
   Expected position: background along the garden path, walking toward the group

EXPECTED OBJECTS (check if present):
- Hausgarten mit Zaun
- Schatzkiste
- Abschlusszettel
- Schokoriegel



COORDINATE SYSTEM:
- Values are 0-1000 (Gemini native format)
- Origin is top-left corner
- Format: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]

FIGURE COUNT LIMIT:
- Return AT MOST 10 figures total. If the scene has a crowd in the background, do NOT enumerate each crowd member as a separate figure — the crowd is backdrop, not a list.
- Only include a figure if its face OR body occupies at least ~5% of the frame width or height. Tiny silhouettes in the distance are backdrop, skip them.
- If you cannot distinguish between several figures (e.g. multiple blurred robes in the background), return ONE figure representing the group and set `name: "UNKNOWN"`, `label: "background crowd"` — never duplicate the same label across many entries.

FOR EACH FIGURE (up to 10, including partially visible ones near the edges of main subjects):
- If you can identify it as an expected character, set "name" to the character name (EXACTLY as listed above)
- Use CLOTHING + POSITION to distinguish figures (two figures with similar build are distinguished by what they wear and where they stand)
- If not identifiable as any expected character, set "name" to "UNKNOWN"
- Include "confidence": "high", "medium", or "low" for identification certainty

  * The face_box should be roughly square for a front-facing figure
- body_box: bounding box around the FULL FIGURE (or as much as visible)
- If the head is not visible (back view, non-human creature), set face_box to null

FOR EXPECTED OBJECTS:
- Report "found": true/false for each expected object

- Every `label` field MUST be ≤ 10 words.

frontCover.prompt:
Generate a SINGLE illustration filling the ENTIRE canvas edge-to-edge. No borders, no frames, no margins, no white edges. No split screen, no panels, no grid, no collage. The artwork must extend to all four edges. All surfaces in the scene — walls, shutters, vehicles, garments, paper, screens, pole-mounted boards, shopfronts — render free of written characters, letters, numbers, or symbols, unless the scene description explicitly names the text to show.

Create a front cover illustration for a children's book.

**SCENE:**
Wonder and discovery. A wide group portrait set before Hausgarten mit Zaun. Emma, 5-year-old female, stands in the left foreground, kneeling on the garden lawn, holds the Schatzkiste, eyes on the Schatzkiste. Noah, 7-year-old male, stands in the right foreground, kneeling beside Emma, holds the ART006, eyes on Emma.

**CHARACTER REFERENCE PHOTOS (one per character, labeled images attached below):** [Emma], [Noah]

**HEIGHT ORDER (shortest to tallest):** Emma (shortest) -> Noah (taller)

**ART STYLE:** A traditional watercolor painting in the style of Inga Moore. Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults. Textured paper with pencil underpainting, delicate color washes with wet-on-wet technique, soft paint edges, visible artistic brushstrokes, and luminous flowing colors. Characters are fully opaque — never see-through, never fading into the background. Warm but not overly vibrant color palette with visible paper texture throughout. Faces: watercolor wash rendering with visible brushstroke texture, age-appropriate features with defined bone structure. Eyes naturally sized. Never sharp or digitally rendered.

**COMPOSITION GUIDELINES:**
- ALL MAIN CHARACTERS should be prominently featured and clearly recognizable
- Characters should be arranged in a balanced composition (side by side, or grouped naturally)
- Keep the composition simple and uncluttered
- Leave clear space at the TOP for the title text
- Each character has 2 hands. Show at most 2 items held per character — if more are mentioned, drop the rest.

**TITLE:**
Paint "Noahs größte Überraschung" in the upper third of the canvas as three-dimensional letters that sit as physical objects in the scene, catching its lighting and shadows. Hand-crafted lettering style fitting the story's world, never standard computer fonts. The only text in the image. Painted on the illustration, not in a band, strip, or caption area outside it.

**FRAMING:**
Borderless full-bleed illustration. No torn-paper border, polaroid frame, scrapbook page, deckle edges, or matte around the artwork.

**KEY STORY ELEMENTS:**
**Erster Hinweiszettel** (artifact): A palm-sized square of white paper, folded once in half, with large wobbly handwritten black ink letters visible when unfolded; slightly creased at the fold
**Versiegelter Umschlag** (artifact): A small cream-coloured paper envelope roughly 10 cm wide, sealed shut with a round red wax stamp on the back flap; no writing on the front
**Sarahs Notiz** (artifact): A fist-sized torn scrap of white notepad paper with neat blue ballpoint handwriting in two short lines; one corner has a small strip of transparent tape where it was attached to the door frame

bboxDetection.rawPrompt:
Detect the 2d bounding boxes of all figures and objects in this illustrated image.

EXPECTED CHARACTERS (identify by name if found):
1. Emma - Emma is a preschooler little girl (Looks: preschooler), average build. Hair: brown, wavy, ear-length, ponytail, side part right, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips, freckles, small stud earrings
2. Noah - Noah is a kindergartner little boy (Looks: kindergartner), average build. Hair: blonde, wavy, ear-length, bangs at eyebrows, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips

(No expected objects provided)



COORDINATE SYSTEM:
- Values are 0-1000 (Gemini native format)
- Origin is top-left corner
- Format: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]

FIGURE COUNT LIMIT:
- Return AT MOST 10 figures total. If the scene has a crowd in the background, do NOT enumerate each crowd member as a separate figure — the crowd is backdrop, not a list.
- Only include a figure if its face OR body occupies at least ~5% of the frame width or height. Tiny silhouettes in the distance are backdrop, skip them.
- If you cannot distinguish between several figures (e.g. multiple blurred robes in the background), return ONE figure representing the group and set `name: "UNKNOWN"`, `label: "background crowd"` — never duplicate the same label across many entries.

FOR EACH FIGURE (up to 10, including partially visible ones near the edges of main subjects):
- If you can identify it as an expected character, set "name" to the character name (EXACTLY as listed above)
- Use CLOTHING + POSITION to distinguish figures (two figures with similar build are distinguished by what they wear and where they stand)
- If not identifiable as any expected character, set "name" to "UNKNOWN"
- Include "confidence": "high", "medium", or "low" for identification certainty
- face_box: bounding box around the head region.
  Include the top of the head and the bottom of the head outline, and the full width from side to side.
  Common mistakes to AVOID:
  * Do NOT cut off the top of the head — include the full head outline
  * Do NOT cut off the bottom of the head outline
  * Do NOT make the box too narrow — include the full head width
  * When in doubt, make the face_box LARGER rather than smaller
  * The face_box should be roughly square for a front-facing figure
- body_box: bounding box around the FULL FIGURE (or as much as visible)
- If the head is not visible (back view, non-human creature), set face_box to null

FOR EXPECTED OBJECTS:
- Report "found": true/false for each expected object
- If found, include body_box bounding box and position

LABEL LENGTH RULE (non-negotiable):
- Every `label` field MUST be ≤ 10 words.
- Name ONE defining clothing item + ONE distinguishing feature. Example: "boy in blue hoodie with backpack".
- DO NOT list everything the figure is wearing. DO NOT describe actions. DO NOT describe expressions.
- Long labels waste response tokens and cause the JSON to truncate before closing.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "figures": [
    {
      "name": "CharacterName or UNKNOWN",
      "label": "≤10 words — one defining item + one distinguishing feature",
      "position": "left|center|right",

      "label": "visual description if found",
      "position": "left|center|right",
      "body_box": [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] or null
    }
  ]
}

EXAMPLE - Scene with two figures and a dog:
Given expected characters: "CharacterA (figure with blonde hair)" and "CharacterB (figure with brown curly hair)"
Given expected objects: "golden crown", "brown teddy bear"

**CHARACTER REFERENCE PHOTOS (one per character, labeled images attached below):** [Emma], [Noah]

Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults.
